'''Gerhard Rambold''' (born 1956) is a German [[lichenology|lichenologist]], [[mycology|mycologist]] and university professor who has led the mycology group at the [[University of Bayreuth]] since 1999. He is recognised for creating LIAS, "A Global Information System for Lichenised and Non‑Lichenised Ascomycetes", which integrates [[morphology (biology)|morphological]], [[molecular phylogenetics|molecular]] and distributional data into interactive identification tools. Combining extensive field collections with [[bioinformatics|bio‑]] and [[ecoinformatics]], his research spans [[taxonomy (biology)|taxonomy]], {{lichengloss|photobiont}} ecology and fungal [[biodiversity]] on several continents.

==Early life and education==

Rambold was born in [[Pocking]], [[Lower Bavaria]] in 1956. He grew up in a musically oriented family in southern Germany but gravitated toward biology while studying at [[LMU Munich]] under the influence of [[Hannes Hertel]].<ref name="Kärnefelt 2009"/> He earned a biology diploma in 1984 with a thesis on rock-dwelling {{lichengloss|lecideoid}} lichens from Iceland, demonstrating an early commitment to meticulous specimen work.<ref name="Hertel et al. 2017"/>

Under Hertel's supervision he completed a doctorate in 1989, producing a [[monograph]] on Australian saxicolous lecideoid lichens based largely on specimens he gathered during an extensive collecting trip across the continent.<ref name="Hertel et al. 2017"/> His [[habilitation]] in [[systematic botany]] followed in 1997 at [[Munich]], concentrating on inter‑[[Lecanorales|lecanoralean]] associations and launching a productive collaboration with his partner Dagmar Triebel.<ref name="Kärnefelt et al. 2012"/>

==Career and research==

Between 1995 and 1998 Rambold lectured at both the [[Technical University of Munich]] and LMU before accepting a full professorship at [[Bayreuth]] in 1999, where he founded the modern mycology section.<ref name="Hertel et al. 2017"/> He simultaneously headed the university's Central Laboratory for DNA Analytics and Ecoinformatics until 2015, embedding [[molecular phylogenetics|molecular]] methods and [[data management]] into lichenological training and infrastructure.<ref name="Kärnefelt et al. 2012"/>

Rambold's interest in [[bioinformatics]] led to LIAS ("A Global Information System for Lichenised and Non‑Lichenised Ascomycetes"), which links taxonomic concepts, {{lichengloss|character}} definitions and checklist data with multilingual, web‑based keys and dynamic distribution maps.<ref name="Hertel et al. 2017"/> The system has become a reference model for biodiversity information platforms and underpins numerous identification programmes worldwide.<ref name="Kärnefelt et al. 2012"/>

His laboratory has explored photobiont specificity, [[terricolous lichen|soil lichen]] diversity in Southern Africa and the [[molecular ecology]] of [[symbiosis|symbiotic]] fungi, producing influential studies such as the 1998 ''[[The Bryologist|Bryologist]]'' paper on photobionts as phylogenetic indicators and subsequent surveys of [[aridity|arid]]‑zone lichen communities.<ref name="Kärnefelt et al. 2012"/> He co‑edited the 2004 [[Festschrift]] "Contributions to Lichenology" honouring Hertel and has supervised doctoral candidates including Andreas Beck, [https://species.wikimedia.org/wiki/Marcela_Eugenia_da_Silva_C%C3%A1ceres Marcela Eugenia da Silva Cáceres], [[Gregor Hagedorn]], Alexandra Kehl and Derek Peršoh.<ref name="Kärnefelt et al. 2012"/>

Rambold is a regular speaker at international meetings—such as the 2004 fifth [[International Association for Lichenology]] congress in Tartu—and collaborates on projects that standardise fungal trait data for [[ecosystem model|ecological modelling]] and conservation planning.<ref name="Kärnefelt 2009"/> He is a section editor for the academic journals ''[[Mycological Progress]]''<ref name="MP page"/> and ''[[MycoKeys]]''.<ref name="MycoKeys"/>

Since 2017 he is member and chair of the International Training Centre for Environmental Research (ITCER) in Kenya.<ref name="ITCER Homepage">{{cite web |title=International Training Centre for Environmental Research |url=https://itcer.org/ |website=ITCER |access-date=29 August 2026}}</ref> Rambold coordinates major projects, with a focus on Africa.<ref name="ITCER Newsletter 1, 2025">{{cite journal |last1=International Training Centre for Environmental Research |title=ITCER Newsletter 1 – October 2025 |journal=Zenodo |date=26 October 2025 |page=1-12 |doi=10.5281/ZENODO.17446672 |url=https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.17446672 |access-date=29 August 2026}}</ref><ref name="ITCER Newsletter 2, 2026">{{cite journal |last1=International Training Centre for Environment Research |title=ITCER Newsletter 2 – June 2026 |journal=Zenodo |date=30 June 2026 |page=1-6 |doi=10.5281/ZENODO.21081134 |url=https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21081134 |access-date=29 August 2026}}</ref>

==Eponyms==

Several taxa have been [[eponym|named to honour]] Rambold.<ref name="Hertel et al. 2017"/> These include the lichen genus ''[[Ramboldia]]'' {{au|Kantvilas & Elix 1994}},<ref name="Kantvilas 1994"/> the lichen species ''[[Relicina ramboldii]]'' {{au|Elix & J.Johnst. (1988)}};<ref name="Elix 1988"/> ''[[Xanthoparmelia gerhardii]]'' {{au|Elix & J.Johnst. (1988)}};<ref name="Elix 1988"/> ''[[Rimularia ramboldiana]]'' {{au|Kantvilas & Elix (2007)}}; ''[[Sculptolumina ramboldii]]'' {{au|Elix & H.Mayrhofer (2018)}},<ref name="Elix & Mayrhofer 2018"/> ''[[Rinodina gerhardii]]'' {{au|H.Mayrhofer & Elix (2020)}};<ref name="Mayrhofer & Elix 2020"/> ''[[Tremella ramboldiae]]'' {{au|Diederich & W.R.Buck (2022)}};<ref name="Diederich et al. 2022"/> the subspecies ''[[Lecanora subimmersa]]'' subsp. ''ramboldii'' {{au|Lumbsch & Elix (1994)}};<ref name="Lumbsch et al. 1994"/> as well as the two spider taxa ''[[Megateg ramboldi]]'' {{au|Raven & Stumkat (2005)}}<ref name="Raven & Stumkat 2005"/> and ''[[Spinasteron ramboldi]]'' {{au|[[Barbara Baehr|Baehr]] & Churchill (2003)}}.<ref name="Baehr & Churchill 2003"/>
